Game.doc: The handler being defined. Set options on it at the top level of the file; define `Game.Play` to customise each instance.

Hub.doc: Hub metadata (filled in when published on hub.splitscreen.me).

Nucleus.doc: The `Nucleus.Gaming` .NET namespace: enums such as `Nucleus.Folder` and helper classes such as `Nucleus.IniSaveInfo`.

Context.doc: Per-instance context. Only available inside `Game.Play` and other callbacks.

Player.doc: The player whose instance is being set up. Only available inside `Game.Play` and other callbacks.

PlayerList.doc: All players of the session (`PlayerList.Count`). Only available inside callbacks.

Handler.doc: The running `GenericGameHandler`. Only available inside callbacks.

ProtoInput.doc: Proto Input runtime API (install hooks, toggle message filters). Only available inside callbacks such as `Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked`.

Hub.doc: Hub metadata, filled in by hub.splitscreen.me when the handler is published.

Hook.doc: Settings for Nucleus' custom xinput/x360ce hook DLL.

SaveType.doc: Not used but could be present in some handlers

SavePath.doc: Not used but could be present in some handlers

DirSymlinkExclusions.doc: Array with the name of the folders you don't want Nucleus Co-op to symlink, only the folders placed here get hardcopied not the files.

FileSymlinkExclusions.doc: Array with the name of the files you don't want Nucleus Co-op to symlink, useful if you want to replace files or add external files.

FileSymlinkCopyInstead.doc: Array with the name of the files you want Nucleus Co-op to make full copies of, in some cases games need certain files to be full copies or they won't run.

DirSymlinkCopyInstead.doc: Copy (not symlink) all files within a given folder | Folder name is relative from root game folder.

DirExclusions.doc: Folders (+ all its contents) listed here will not be linked or copied over to Nucleus game content folder, the instance folders.

KeepSymLinkOnExit.doc: Enable or disable symlink files from being deleted when Nucleus is closed | default: false.

HandlerInterval.doc: The interval in milliseconds the Handler should be updated at. Set it to 0 to disable updating (will lose all functionality that depends on ticks).

Debug.doc: Writes a detailed debug log while the handler runs.

SupportsPositioning.doc: Chooses whether or not to automatically move the windows around to fit in the right spaces.

SymlinkExe.doc: If SymlinkGame is enabled, if we should copy or symlink the game executable.

SymlinkGame.doc: If we should symbolic link the game's files to a temporary directory (Nucleus instances folders in its content folder). If not will launch straight from the installation directory.

HardcopyGame.doc: Instead of Symlinking, create hard copies of the games files (copy/paste) | Be careful of storage, takes a LONG time to start a game when copying.

SupportsKeyboard.doc: Enable/disable use of one keyboard/mouse player.

KeyboardPlayerFirst.doc: If the keyboard player should be processed first.

ExecutableContext.doc: Array with the name of other files found in the executable's folder (so we don't confuse different games with similar file names). Example: Borderlands and Tales of the Borderlands share their executable name (borderlands.exe). We include 1 folder and a file that's unique to Borderlands to make sure the application doesn't confuse itself.

ExecutableNames.doc: Alternative executable names this handler matches (e.g. different store versions).

ExecutableName.doc: The name of the game executable with the extension. This will be used by Nucleus to add games, to run the game and as process to follow for positioning and resizing.

SteamID.doc: Here the SteamID of the game. You can find it on https://steamdb.info/ . Add only if the game is available on Steam.

GUID.doc: The name of the folder that will be created inside the Nucleus content folder (just use letters not symbols). In this folder Nucleus will store the symlinked or copied game files for each instance of the game.

GameName.doc: Title of the game that will be shown in Nucleus.

MaxPlayers.doc: This is just the max players info that shows under the handler name in Nucleus UI. Usually we write the max number of players the game supports. (PC, should support 16 max connected input devices).

MaxPlayersOneMonitor.doc: This is just info. It will not limit the players number.

PauseBetweenStarts.doc: Pause between game intances starts in milliseconds.

DPIHandling.doc: The way the games handles DPI scaling. Modify this if the game is presenting different sizing behaviour after the Windows 10 Creators Update. Values: True: True tries to send the correct width and height to the game's window. Nucleus.DPIHandling.Scaled: Scaled will scale the width and height by the DPI of the system (see that it's not per-monitor). Nucleus.DPIHandling.InvScaled: InvScaled will scale the width and height by 1 / DPI of the system (see that it's not per-monitor).

StartArguments.doc: Adds whatever you put into the field as starting parameters for the game's executable. For example, in most cases '-windowed' will force windowed mode. Parameters can be chained. Necessary for some games.

BinariesFolder.doc: In which folder the game exe is located? Relative path to where Nucleus should start the game's working folder to.

FakeFocus.doc: Enable or disable the sending of focus messages to each game window at a regular interval | default: false.

FakeFocusInterval.doc: The milliseconds between sending fake focus messages. Default at 1000, some rare games need this to be very low.

FakeFocusSendActivate.doc: Should WM_ACTIVATE message be sent to each instance? | default: true.

SplitDivCompatibility.doc: Explicitly disable splitscreen divisons if the game is known to be imcompatible with it.(Does not require to be true for compatible game)Default = true.

SetTopMostAtEnd.doc: Set the game windows to top most at the very end.

AddOption.doc: Adds a user-selectable option to the game profile. Read it back in `Game.Play` with `Context.Options["key"]`.

WorkingFolder.doc: Relative path to where Nucleus should start the game's working folder to. Example: The main executable is on the root directory (left4dead2.exe), but the game expects to be started with a working folder of 'bin' (all the game's libraries are there).

NeedsSteamEmulation.doc: If the game needs a fake Steam wrapper (SSE) to run multiple instances (this is not needed if you are using the new use Goldberg emulator line).

KillMutex.doc: Array of mutexes to kill before starting the next game process. A 'Mutex/Mutant' is a mutually exclusive flag, which basically tells the game not to allow multiple instances of its program.

KillMutexType.doc: Specify the type of mutex/handle to kill, for example "Mutant", "Event" or "Semaphore" | default: "Mutant".

KillMutexDelay.doc: \# of seconds to wait before killing the mutex | Only works with killing not renaming | default: 0.

LauncherExe.doc: If the game needs to go through a launcher before opening Nucleus will use this exe to start the game and it will still use the Game.ExecutableName process for positioning and resizing.

LauncherTitle.doc: The name of the launcher's window title. Some games need to go through a launcher to open. This is needed or else the application will lose the game's window.

Play.doc: Called once per instance, right before the game process is started. `Context`, `Player`, `PlayerList` and `Handler` are available inside this function.

SetupSse.doc: Called to set up Smart Steam Emulator.

OnStop.doc: Called when the session is stopped.

OnFinishedSetup.doc: Called once all instances have been set up.

LockMouse.doc: If we should lock the mouse, requires Game.Hook.CustomDllEnabled = true;.

Folder.doc: Path to the game handler folder (Nucleus-Coop\handlers\handler_folder).

HookFocus.doc: Enable or disable hooks to trick the game into thinking it has focus | default: false.

ForceWindowTitle.doc: Forces the game window title to be whatever is specified in Game.Hook.ForceFocusWindowName (triggers once, after all instances have started) | default: false.

IdealProcessor.doc: Sets the preferred processor for the game's threads, used when the system schedules threads, to determine which processor to run the thread on | default: system delegation.

UseProcessor.doc: Sets the processors on which the game's threads can run on (provide the # of the cores in a comma-seperated list in quotations) | default: system delegation.

ProcessorPriorityClass.doc:
Game.WriteToProcessMemory 				//(undocumented)
Sets the overall priority category for the associated process. Can be "AboveNormal", "High" or "RealTime" | default: "Normal".

CMDLaunch.doc: Launch a game using command prompt.

CMDOptions.doc: Specify command line options if game is launched using command prompt | requires CMDLaunch to be true, each element is for a different instance.

HasDynamicWindowTitle.doc: Work-around for ForceFocusWindowName having to match 1:1 with game window title for resizing, positioning and focus | default: false.

SymlinkFiles.doc: Symlink individual files from the game directory to the instanced folder.

HookInit.doc: Enable or disable hooks of functions some games may try and use to prevent multiple instances from running | default: false.

CopyFiles.doc: Copy files from the game directory to the instanced folder.

SetWindowHook.doc: Prevent games from resizing their windows on their own | Hooks after all instances have been opened (see Game.SetWindowHookStart for an alternative).

HideTaskbar.doc: Most games hide the taskbar when placed on-top but for games that don't you can use this.

PromptBetweenInstances.doc: Prompt the user with a messagebox to let the user decide when to open the next instance | default: false, PauseBetweenStarts STILL required.

HideCursor.doc: Hide the mouse cursor in game instances.

RenameNotKillMutex.doc: Instead of killing the mutex or handle, rename it on startup to something else | Requires Game.KillMutex to contain the EXACT name of the handles for this to work (no partial).

IdInWindowTitle.doc: Adds the process ID to the end of the window title.

ChangeExe.doc: Will rename the game's executable to "\<exe name\> - Player X", x being the instance/player #.

UseX360ce.doc: Before launching any games, Nucleus Co-op will open x360ce and let the user set up their controllers before continuing | close x360ce to continue | Don't use with custom dlls.

KeepAspectRatio.doc: Should the game window try and keep it's aspect ratio when being resized? | default: false.

HideDesktop.doc: Hide the desktop background with a solid black background.

ResetWindows.doc: After each new instance opens, resize, reposition and remove borders of the previous instance.

PartialMutexSearch.doc: When killing handles, should a partial search be done with the handle name? | Renaming handles requires an exact match | default: false.

UseGoldberg.doc: Use the built-in Goldberg features in Nucleus | default: false.

OrigSteamDllPath.doc: If steam_interface.txt is required, provide full path here to the original steam_api(64).dll and Nucleus will create one if it can't find an existing copy.

GoldbergNeedSteamInterface.doc: Some older games require a steam_interfaces.txt file for Goldberg to work | Will first search orig game path and nucleus games path, if not found then tries to create one with the GoldbergNeedSteamInterface command.

UseSteamless.doc: Use atom0s' Steamless app to remove Steam Stub DRM from a protected executable.

SteamlessArgs.doc: Use this when using Game.UseSteamless = true; always, the command line version of Steamless allows for different launch arguments to be used.

SteamlessTiming.doc: The time in milliseconds to give Steamless to patch the game .exe. 2500 is the default value and will be applied even if the timing line has not been added in a handler.

SteamlessPatch.doc: bool apply to launcher,string Steamless Args,int wait for exe patching finished.

XboxOneControllerFix.doc: When using x360ce, this will set certain hooktype that may work for xbox one controllers if the normal method does not work.

UseForceBindIP.doc: Set up game instances with ForceBindIP; each instance having their own IP.

XInputPlusDll.doc: Set up XInputPlus | If multiple dlls required, use comma seperated strings.

SDLPaths.doc: Relative to instanced game directory root

CopyCustomUtils.doc: Copy a file or folder you specify between the quotes to each instance folder, if the file/folder is located in Nucleus folder\utils\User. This function also accepts two additional parameters, a relative path from the game root folder if the file needs to be placed somewhere else within instance folder and one parameter to indicate which instances to copy the file to if it only needs to be in some. Use of parameters is separated by a | character. So it would look something like this [ "filename.ini|\\bin|1,2" ]. This example would copy filename.ini from Nucleus\utils\User to Instance0\bin and Instance1\bin. If you don't specify which instances, it will do them all by default. If you don't specify a path then root instance folder is used. If you want instances but root folder you would just do [ "filename.ini||1,2" ] | If copying multiple files, use comma seperated strings

PlayersPerInstance.doc: If using XInputPlus or X360ce and there are multiple players playing the same instance, set the # per instance here.

HexEditAllExes.doc: Will do a text value replacement in a file for every instance, accepts two parameters, one on what to look for, and what it should be replaced with (seperated with a "|") | Works with multiple values | Works in conjunction with HexEditExe (this will trigger first).

HexEditExe.doc: Will do a text value replacement in a file for a specific instance, accepts two parameters, one on what to look for, and what it should be replaced with (seperated with a "|") | Works with multiple values, each comma seperated string is the order of the instances | Works in conjunction with HexEditAllExe (this will trigger second).

BlockRawInput.doc: Disable raw input devices in game | default: false.

HexEditFile.doc: Works same as HexEditExe function but with a file you specify as an extra parameter (first one) | filePath is relative path from the game root folder.

HexEditAllFiles.doc: Works same as HexEditAllExes function but with a file you specify as an extra parameter (first one) | filePath is relative path from the game root folder.

SetWindowHookStart.doc: Prevent games from resizing window their windows on their own | Hooks upon game starting up (see Game.SetWindowHook for an alternative).

GoldbergLanguage.doc: Manually specify what language you want Goldberg to use for the game | by default, Goldberg will use the language you chose in Steam.

Description.doc: Display a message to the end-user, that will appear when user selects the game of a handler| useful if there is anything the end-user needs to know before-hand | Only first two or three sentences will appear in UI, but full message can be viewed if user right clicks on the game in the list.

GoldbergExperimental.doc: Use the experimental branch of Goldberg | Requires `Game.UseGoldberg = true` | default: false.

GoldbergIgnoreSteamAppId.doc: When set to true, Goldberg will not create a steam_appid.txt file.

UseSteamStubDRMPatcher.doc: Use UberPsyX's Steam Stub DRM Patcher to remove Steam Stub DRM from a protected executable.

HardlinkGame.doc: Hardlink files instead of Symlink (or hard copy) | Directories will still be symlinked but files will be hardlinked.

SetForegroundWindowElsewhere.doc: Set the foreground window to be something other than game windows.

PreventWindowDeactivation.doc: Blocks the processing of all the windows messages that get sent when the window loses focus.

SymlinkFolders.doc: Folders by default are hardcopied, with this enabled, folders will be symlinked instead | warning files placed in symlink folders will appear in the original game files too.

CreateSteamAppIdByExe.doc: Create a steam_appid.txt file where the game executable is.

ForceSymlink.doc: Force game to be symlinked each time it is ran.

UseProcessorsPerInstance.doc: Sets the processors on which an instances game's threads can run on (provide the # of the cores in a comma-seperated list in quotations) | default: system delegation.

UseDirectX9Wrapper.doc: Use a Direct X wrapper to try and force DirectX 9 games to run windowed.

SteamStubDRMPatcherArch.doc: Force Steam Stub DRM Patcher to use either the x64 or x86 dll | Values: "64" or "86".

GoldbergLobbyConnect.doc: Should Goldberg Lobby Connect be used to connect the instances.

X360ceDll.doc: If x360ce dll should be named something OTHER than xinput1_3.dll | requires Game.Usex360ce to be set to true.

CMDBatchBefore.doc: When using CMDLaunch (or UseForceBindIP), specify command lines to run BEFORE the game launches in same cmd session, syntax is instance and | symbol as a delimiter and the line you want that instance to run. If you want same line to run all instances, leave out the # and | (only write the line in quotes).

CMDBatchAfter.doc: When using CMDLaunch (or UseForceBindIP), specify command lines to run AFTER the game launches in same cmd session, syntax is instance and | symbol as a delimiter and the line you want that instance to run. If you want same line to run all instances, leave out the # and | (only write the line in quotes).

GoldbergNoLocalSave.doc: Do not create a local_save.txt file for Goldberg, saves are to use default game save location.

UseNucleusEnvironment.doc: Use custom environment variables for games that use them, replaces some common paths (e.g. AppData) with C:\Users\\<your username\>\NucleusCoop.

ThirdPartyLaunch.doc: Use if the game is launched outside of Nucleus | NOTE: You will not be able to use start up hooks or CMDLaunch with this option.

ForceProcessPick.doc: Manually select the process that will be used for process manipulation, such as resizing, repositioning and used for post-launch hooks.

KeepMonitorAspectRatio.doc: Try and resize game window within player bounds to the aspect ratio of the monitor.

PostHookInstances.doc: If you only want specific instances to have post launch hooks, specify them in a comma seperated string.

StartHookInstances.doc: If you only want specific instances to have starting hooks, specify them in a comma seperated string.

FakeFocusInstances.doc: If you only want specific instances to have fake focus messages sent to, specify them in a comma seperated string.

KeyboardPlayerSkipFakeFocus.doc: Should the keyboard player instance be skipped when fake focus messages are being sent to.

UserProfileConfigPath.doc: Relative path from user profile (e.g. C:\Users\ZeroFox) to game's config path | Used to provide some extra functionality (open/delete/copy over to Nucleus Environment).

UserProfileSavePath.doc: Relative path from user profile (e.g. C:\Users\ZeroFox) to game's save path | Used to provide some extra functionality (open/delete/copy over to Nucleus Environment).

PlayerSteamIDs.doc: A list of steam IDs to be used instead of the pre-defined ones Nucleuses uses | IDs will be used in order they are placed, i.e. instance 1 will be first non-empty string in array.

HexEditExeAddress.doc: Use this to replace bytes in a file at a specified address, can be for specific instances with optional 3rd argument | 1st arg: instance # (optional), 2nd arg: hex address offset, 3rd arg: new bytes.

ForceUserProfileConfigCopy.doc: Force the games config files in UserProfileConfigPath to copy over from system user profile to Nucleus environment.

ForceUserProfileSaveCopy.doc: Force the games save files in UserProfileSavePath to copy over from system user profile to Nucleus environment.

ProcessChangesAtEnd.doc: Do the resizing, repositioning and post-launch hooking of all game instances at the very end | will not work with every option ran normally.

PromptProcessChangesAtEnd.doc: If ProcessChangesAtEnd = true, pause and show a prompt, before making changes to processes.

DeleteFilesInConfigPath.doc: Specify files to delete in Nucleus environment config path (UserProfileConfigPath).

DeleteFilesInSavePath.doc: Specify files to delete in Nucleus environment save path (UserProfileSavePath).

PromptBetweenInstancesEnd.doc: If ProcessChangesAtEnd = true, show a prompt between each instance being changed.

Game.HexEditFileAddress = [ "1|relativePath|address|bytes" ]; //Same as HexEditExeAddress but for a file other than exe | Need to provide relative path (from game root folder) + filename as 1st or 2nd arg if not specifying an instance.
Do not display the warning message about a file being deleted .

ChangeIPPerInstance.doc: Highly experimental feature, will change your existing network to a static IP for each instance | option in settings to choose your network.

FlawlessWidescreen.doc: Use Flawless Widescreen application | value must be the name of the game plugin folder in PluginCache\FWS_Plugins\Modules.

DeleteFiles.doc:
Game.RenameAndOrMoveFiles = [ "1|before.dat|after.dat" ];//Specify files to either rename or move | can accept relative path from root | optional first parameter to specify a specific instance to apply to, omit to do them all.
Specify files to be deleted from instanced folder | can accept relative path from root | optional first parameter to specify a specific instance to apply to, omit to do them all.

GoldbergExperimentalRename.doc: Set to true to have Goldberg Experimental rename instanced steam_api(64).dll to cracksteam_api(64).dll.

KillProcessesOnClose.doc: List of additional processes that need to be killed (other than executable and launcher).

KeyboardPlayerSkipPreventWindowDeactivat.doc: Ignore PreventWindowDeactivation if player is using keyboard.

DontResize.doc: Should Nucleus not resize the game windows?.

DontReposition.doc: Should Nucleus not reposition the game windows?.

NotTopMost.doc: Should Nucleus not make the game windows top most (appear above everything else).

WindowStyleValues.doc: docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-styles for values that can be used.

ExtWindowStyleValues.doc: docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-styles for values that can be used.

KillLastInstanceMutex.doc: Kill the handles, specified in Game.KillMutex, in the last instance (normally last is ignored).

RefreshWindowAfterStart.doc: Should each game window be minimized and restored once all instances are opened?.

CreateSingleDeviceFile.doc: Create only one file for HID devices per instance (the assigned HID device).

KillMutexAtEnd.doc: When using ProcessChangesAtEnd, should handles also be killed at the end?.

When using CMDLaunch, should the game's starting arguments be inside the same quotations as the game path?

UseEACBypass.doc: Replace any EasyAntiCheat_(x86)(x64).dll with a bypass dll.

LaunchAsDifferentUsers.doc: Launch each instance from a different user account | must run Nucleus as admin | will temporary create user accounts "nucleusplayerx" and delete them when closing Nucleus.

RunLauncherAndExe.doc:
When using Game.LauncherExe, should ExecutableName also be launched?
Forces LauncherExeIgnoreFileCheck when game isn't symlinked.

PauseBetweenProcessGrab.doc: How many seconds to wait after launching game (or launcher) but before grabbing game process.

PauseBetweenContextAndLaunch.doc: Number of seconds to wait after running additional files but before continuing with player setup.

DirSymlinkCopyInsteadIncludeSubFolders.doc: When specifying folder(s) to copy all its contents instead of linking, should subfolders and files be included as well?

LaunchAsDifferentUsersAlt.doc: An alternative method to launch each instance from a different user account | must run Nucleus as admin | will temporary create user accounts "nucleusplayerx" and delete them when closing Nucleus.

UserProfileConfigPathNoCopy.doc: Do not copy files from original UserProfileConfigPath if using Nucleus Environment.

UserProfileSavePathNoCopy.doc: Do not copy files from original UserProfileSavePath if using Nucleus Environment.

LauncherExeIgnoreFileCheck.doc: Do not check if Launcher Exe exists in game folder | you will need to provide a relative filepath from game root folder.

CustomUserGeneralPrompts.doc: This prompts user one time and applies to ALL players, unless a value text file already exists and saving is on.

CustomUserPlayerPrompts.doc: This will prompt each player, unless a value text file already exists for that player and saving for players is on.
CustomUserPlayerPrompts.example: Game.CustomUserPlayerPrompts = ["Enter network Adapter name", "Enter character name"];

CustomUserInstancePrompts.doc: This will prompt each instance, unless a value text file already exists for that instance and save is on. In case it is not player specific but different values are needed for instances.

TransferNucleusUserAccountProfiles.doc: Will backup and restore Nucleus user account user profile's on windows between sessions (when user accounts are not kept).

UseCurrentUserEnvironment.doc: Force the game to use the current user's environment (useful for some games that may require different Window user accounts).

EnableWindows.doc: Enable each game window at the end (useful if became disabled, or for some games that require this Window function to be called to display properly, after Nucleus setup).

WindowStyleEndChanges.doc: docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-styles for values that can be used.

ExtWindowStyleEndChanges.doc: docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/winmsg/window-styles for values that can be used.

UseDInputBlocker.doc: Setup wizark952's dinput blocker (block dinput for the game).

IgnoreThirdPartyPrompt.doc: Ignore the prompt that appears when using Game.ThirdPartyLaunch;

ExecutableToLaunch.doc: If the game is to launch a different executable, other than what Game.ExecutableName is.

GoldbergWriteSteamIDAndAccount.doc: Force Goldberg to write account_name.txt and user_steam_id.txt | Requires Game.UseGoldberg;

ForceProcessSearch.doc: Force Nucleus to search for the game process.

UseNemirtingasEpicEmu.doc: Automatically set up Nemirtinga's Epic Emulator in Nucleus

UseNemirtingasGalaxyEmu.doc:

AltEpicEmuArgs.doc: Optional. PromptAfterFirstInstance.doc: Show a prompt that user must click on ok to continue, after the first instance is setup.

Copy folders in game root folder to another spot in game folder | Relative paths from root of game folder.

SymlinkFoldersTo.doc: Symlink folders in game root folder to another spot in game folder | Relative paths from root of game folder.

HardlinkFoldersTo.doc: Hardlink folders in game root folder to another spot in game folder | Relative paths from root of game folder.

RequiresAdmin.doc: Game requires Nucleus to be run as administrator (this option will check and advise if detected not running Nucleus as admin).

PauseCMDBatchBefore.doc: Wait for X number of seconds before proceeding with CMDBatchBefore.

PauseCMDBatchAfter.doc: Wait for X number of seconds before proceeding with CMDBatchAfter.

DontRemoveBorders.doc: Prevents Nucleus from removing game window borders.

KillMutexProcess.doc: When using Game.MutexProcessExe, here you can specify the handles that need to be killed.

MutexProcessExe.doc: Specify another executable to kill handles for.

PartialMutexSearchProcess.doc: When using Game.MutexProcessExe, here you can specify if you want to do a partial search for handles.

KillMutexTypeProcess.doc: When using Game.MutexProcessExe, here you can specify the type of handles to kill.

GoldbergExperimentalSteamClient.doc: Automatically setup Goldberg's Experimental Steam Client | Requires Game.UseGoldberg and the original steam_api.dll.

PauseBeforeMutexKilling.doc: Wait for X number of seconds before proceeding with mutex killing.

KillMutexDelayProcess.doc: When using Game.MutexProcessExe, wait for X number of seconds before beginning its mutex killing.

XInputPlusNoIni.doc: Do not copy XInputPlus' ini when using Game.XInputPlusDll.

DocumentsConfigPath.doc: Similar to UserProfileConfigPath, use this when the game uses Documents to store game files.

DocumentsSavePath.doc: Similar to UserProfileSavePath, use this when the game uses Documents to store game files.

ForceDocumentsConfigCopy.doc: When using DocumentsConfigPath, forces a file copy from original location to Nucleus Documents.

ForceDocumentsSaveCopy.doc: When using DocumentsSavePath, forces a file copy from original location to Nucleus Documents.

DocumentsConfigPathNoCopy.doc: When using DocumentsConfigPath, do not let Nucleus copy from original location to Nucleus Documents.

DocumentsSavePathNoCopy.doc: When using DocumentsSavePath, do not let Nucleus copy from original location to Nucleus Documents.

XInputPlusOldDll.doc: When using Game.XInputPlusDll, you can specify to use the previous version instead of latest (needed for some games).

ForceGameArch.doc: Force Nucleus to treat the game as 32 or 64-bit architecture.

SSEAdditionalLines.doc: When using Game.NeedsSteamEmulation, here you can provide additional lines to write to the SSE ini file.

DeleteOnClose.doc: Delete a file upon ending game session | Relative paths from root of game folder.

SupportsMultipleKeyboardsAndMice.doc: If enabled, it will allow multiple Keyboards and Mice to be used as a device input in Nucleus. Before enabling it by default, be sure that all works without problems.
SupportsMultipleKeyboardsAndMice.category: Support for multiple mice and keyboards

HookSetCursorPos.doc:
This will hook the SetCursorPos Windows function which the game may use to set the mouse position. 
 This is useful to have on to prevent the game from moving the 'real' Windows mouse cursor around the screen.
HookSetCursorPos.category: Support for multiple mice and keyboards

HookGetCursorPos.doc: This will hook the GetCursorPos Windows function which the game may use to get the mouse position.
HookGetCursorPos.category: Support for multiple mice and keyboards

HookGetKeyState.doc: These options hook Windows functions that can be used by the game to detect if keys are down.

RegisterRawInputHook.doc: This hook will unsubscribe the game from Raw Input (if it has already subscribed to it), and then subscribes Proto Input to receive raw input instead. Raw input received is forwarded back to the game if it uses raw input. Proto Input receives all keyboard/mouse input from this hook so it always needs to be enabled.

GetRawInputDataHook.doc: When forwarding the input back to the game, you need to create a handle to the input data. However these handles can only be created by Windows. To get around this, Proto Input will send a dummy WM_INPUT message to the game (from the Register Raw Input hook). The game then calls GetRawInputData using the dummy handle. This hook intercepts the call and passes in the saved data. This hook is required to make forwarding raw input work, so it should always be enabled.

MessageFilterHook.doc: Hooks the GetMessage and PeekMessage functions to intercept every windows message for every window owned by the process. (Note this method is superior to changing WndProc since it works for all windows without knowing what they are, and is less fragile). This hook is used to make the message filters and blocks work. This should always be enabled.

GetCursorPosHook.doc: The GetCursorPos is one way of obtaining the cursor position, so this hook redirects it to the "fake" cursor position. Should always be enabled.

SetCursorPosHook.doc: SetCursorPos sets the cursor position. This hook causes it to set the "fake" cursor instead. This is important in some games that will set the mouse cursor to the centre of the screen each frame, then calculate the difference in movement each frame. This hook also prevents moving the "real" cursor, which can be problematic. Should always be enabled.

GetKeyStateHook.doc: Hooks GetKeyState to return the "fake" keyboard state. You should almost always have this enabled even if it appears to have no effect: when using multiple keyboards at the game time, they may interfere without this hook.

GetAsyncKeyStateHook.doc: Similar to Get Key State. Async also tells the caller whether the key was pressed since the last call, so this can resolve issues where keys are pressed or release when they shouldn't. Should almost always be enabled.

GetKeyboardStateHook.doc: Basically the same as Get Key State, except it returns the state of the entire keyboard. Should almost always be enabled.

CursorVisibilityHook.doc: Monitors when the game tries to hide the cursor (e.g. when you close the menu in a first person game), and sets the visibility of the fake cursor instead. Should be almost always be enabled, except sometimes during debugging when you want to see where the fake mouse cursor is at all times. This hook also monitors calls to set the cursor image, so Proto Input will change the fake cursor to match the game's cursor image. Some games (notably Unity engine games) need DontShowCursorWhenImageUpdated enabled or the cursors will show when they shouldn't.

ClipCursorHook.doc: Prevents the game from setting a bounding region about the mouse cursor. Some games will repeatedly clip the cursor when they receive the fake focus, so this should almost always be enabled. Fake clip means that if the game tries to clip (i.e. bound) the real cursor, it will bound the fake cursor instead.

ClipCursorHookCreatesFakeClip.doc: Prevents the game from setting a bounding region about the mouse cursor. Some games will repeatedly clip the cursor when they receive the fake focus, so this should almost always be enabled. Fake clip means that if the game tries to clip (i.e. bound) the real cursor, it will bound the fake cursor instead.

FocusHooks.doc: Hooks many functions (see the Details tab of the hook) related to the game checking if it's in the foreground or focused. Should always be enabled. Proto Input will repeatedly scan to find the main window, in case it changes.

XinputHook.doc: Xinput is used by most games for controller input. This hook changes the controller indexes so each instance can receive input from a different device. The controller index can be set from Nucleus or Proto Input Host, or it can be edited at runtime in the details tab. Xinput by default has a maximum of 4 controllers. This restriction can be removed if you enable use of the Openxinput library. However, this still will only let you use standard xinput controllers (no cheap PS1 controller adapters). If you want to use any device, enable the Dinput to Xinput redirection, which takes input from Direct Input (which supports any controller) and translates it to Xinput in the hook. Usually Openxinput is the best choice since it will work with vibration and using both triggers simultaneously.

DinputDeviceHook.doc:
Some (few) games will use Direct Input instead of Xinput to get controller input. The Direct Input API involves creating an "interface" to receive input from a controller. Typically a game will create this interface at startup for the first or all controllers. This hook will redirect the interface to the GUID of the selected controller. Note that the controller GUID can only be set automatically through Nucleus (not at runtime).
If this method doesn't work, you can also try with DinputHookAlsoHooksGetDeviceState. This will additionally hook the GetDeviceState function, which is called whenever the game polls input. This method is highly un-recommended since there's no guarantee the game expects the data to be formatted in the same way that Proto Input does, which can lead to completely mesesed up input.

SetWindowPosHook.doc: Prevents the game from calling SetWindowPos to resposition and resize the game window, instead forcing it to the resolution set by Nucleus. This will usually require using startup hooks.

BlockRawInputHook.doc: Blocks calls to GetRegisteredRawInputDevices and GetRawInputDeviceList to prevent the game from detecting raw input devices. You will usually need to use startup injection with this hook. If you enable this hook, you should **disable** the raw input filter, and add a block to WM_INPUT, like so: `Game.ProtoInput.BlockedMessages = [ 0x00FF ];`

FindWindowHook.doc: Blocks calls to FindWindow and EnumWindow so the game cannot detect any windows. This is required for opening multiple instances of some games. You will usually need to use startup injection with this hook.

CreateSingleHIDHook.doc: Hooks CreateFile so the game can only open the HID for the selected device (in Nucleus). This will usually require using startup injection.

SetWindowStyleHook.doc: Hooks SetWindowLong and SetWindowLongPtr to prevent the game from re-adding a title bar after Nucleus has stripped it.

RawInputFilter.doc: Filters the WM_INPUT messages (which send raw input data) to only allow the forwarded messages from the Register Raw Input hook. This will allow only input from the selected device(s). Also modifies the message to tell the game that input was received while the game was in the foreground. Should always be enabled.

MouseMoveFilter.doc: One method of getting the mouse position/state is through the WM_MOUSEMOVE message, so this modifies the data to return the "fake" mouse state. ****This filter is not recommended as it can be very CPU intensive (with multiple mice polling at hundreds of Hz), however it is required for input to work in some games.**** Test with it enabled and disabled to check if you require it.

MouseActivateFilter.doc: WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATE and WM_ACTIVATEAPP all tell a window when it's activated or deactivated. These filters modify the messages to make the window think it's in the foreground and activated. Should always be enabled.

WindowActivateFilter.doc: WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATE and WM_ACTIVATEAPP all tell a window when it's activated or deactivated. These filters modify the messages to make the window think it's in the foreground and activated. Should always be enabled.

WindowActvateAppFilter.doc: WM_MOUSEACTIVATE, WM_ACTIVATE and WM_ACTIVATEAPP all tell a window when it's activated or deactivated. These filters modify the messages to make the window think it's in the foreground and activated. Should always be enabled.

MouseWheelFilter.doc: Filters the WM_MOUSEWHEEL messages to only pass "fake" input. This fixes the issue of the foreground window receiving two scrolls for each scroll. Should always be enabled.

MouseButtonFilter.doc: Filters the mouse buttons messages to only pass "fake" input. This prevents any interaction from the "real" mouse cursor with our input. Should always be enabled.

KeyboardButtonFilter.doc: Same as the Mouse Buttons filter, for keyboard buttons. Should always be enabled.

BlockedMessages.doc: Blocks calls to GetRegisteredRawInputDevices and GetRawInputDeviceList to prevent the game from detecting raw input devices. You will usually need to use startup injection with this hook. If you enable this hook, you should **disable** the raw input filter, and add a block to WM_INPUT, like so: `Game.ProtoInput.BlockedMessages = [ 0x00FF ];`

RenameHandles.doc: Some games will use handles (of mutants, events or semaphores) or named pipes to prevent opening multiple instances. New instances will detect the handle opened by the previous instance, then refuse to open. Proto Input gets around this by renaming the handles to something random (e.g. "mutex" to "mutex2733894") so the new instances can't detect it. Since the handles are usually opened at startup, you will usually need startup injection. To get the names of these handles, use Process Explorer to browse the handles, then use some guesswork.

RenameNamedPipes.doc: Some games will use handles (of mutants, events or semaphores) or named pipes to prevent opening multiple instances. Since the handles are usually opened at startup, you will usually need startup injection. To get the names of these handles, use Process Explorer to browse the handles, then use some guesswork.
RenameNamedPipes.example: Game.ProtoInput.RenameNamedPipes = [ "some named pipe", "some other named pipe" ];
